title.narrative: Activating the Power of PCJ 2021-2025

description.narrative: The overall impact of the programme is to empower people and institutions in the targeted countries to prevent or resolve pressing justice problems. This programme is focussed on a selection of seven countries fall under the priority countries for your ministry: Mali, Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya and Tunisia.

The programme try to achieve the following five outcomes:Outcome I - Enhanced access to and use by justice sector stakeholders of data and knowledge about justice needs and outcomes of justice journeysOutcome II - Improved capacity of justice practitioners and providers of justice services to resolve the most pressing justice problemsOutcome III - Increased access to and use of justice services for peopleOutcome IV - Strengthened dialogue between justice stakeholders on justice needs to create the necessary political space and an enabling environment for justice innovation and gamechangersOutcome V - Reinforced international, regional, and national networks of people-centred justice

title.narrative: Number of persons with access to justice

comment.narrative: MoV: start-up self-reporting and due diligence. Data collection method: Justice Accelerator impact survey sent to supported start-ups.

Start of the programme, no outcome level indicators yet. The Actual value remains 0 as this initial period focused entirely on programme setup, partner alignment, and finalizing the first cohort selection (Deviation: Significant shortfall due to programmatic setup lag). Due to methodology constraints at the time, gender and country-level disaggregation for this period is unavailable.
MoV: start-up self-reporting and due diligence. Data collection method: Justice Accelerator impact survey sent to supported start-ups.

Target/Methodology Reconciliation: The Target is set based on the commitment to track cases that are prevented or resolved. The Actual is calculated for resolved cases only (MFA mandate). The Actual of 142,890 is a reduction compared to the previous year, primarily due to a more conservative calculation method and shifts in the supported cohort size. Gender Achievement: We successfully captured and report gender disaggregation, showing that approximately 54% of people reached are women. Data Limitation: Due to programmatic constraints, country-level disaggregation is unavailable. We are also unable to provide disaggregation for sexual violence cases as they fall outside the current scope of the Accelerator's programming.
MoV: start-up self-reporting and due diligence. Data collection method: Justice Accelerator impact survey sent to supported start-ups.

Target/Methodology Reconciliation: The Target is set based on the commitment to track cases that are prevented or resolved. The Actual is calculated for resolved cases only (MFA mandate). The Actual of 184,160 represents a significant overachievement (Deviation: 268% over target), largely driven by the high early impact of the first cohort and the establishment of the methodology. Due to methodology constraints at the time, gender and country-level disaggregation for this period is unavailable.
MoV: start-up self-reporting and due diligence. Data collection method: Justice Accelerator impact survey sent to supported start-ups.

Target/Methodology Reconciliation: The Target is set based on the commitment to track cases that are prevented or resolved. The Actual is calculated for resolved cases only (MFA mandate). The Actual of 203,729 represents a continued strong overachievement (Deviation: 307% over target). This Actual shows a slight 10% increase over the previous year, demonstrating consistent growth in the Justice Accelerator portfolio. Due to methodology constraints at the time, gender and country-level disaggregation for this period is unavailable.

Number of inclusive law and policy reform initiatives advanced.

comment.narrative: Official launch documents, MoUs, government decrees, and HiiL’s final strategy reports (e.g., Justice Transformation Strategy documents) confirming public commitment to the initiative.

One initiative advanced (Actual: 1). The Justice Transformation Lab (JTL) process was completed in Imo State, Nigeria, resulting in the launch of a new Justice Transformation Strategy (Output 4.4) for the state.
Official launch documents, MoUs, government decrees, and HiiL’s final strategy reports (e.g., Justice Transformation Strategy documents) confirming public commitment to the initiative.

Target was achieved. Five key policy/strategic documents were advanced: Four in Uganda ('the Judiciary Alternative Justice System (AJS) strategy for the Judiciary of Uganda June 2023', 'National Alternative Dispute Resolution Policy 2023', 'Access to justice Sub programme strategic plan 2020/2021-2024 /2025', and 'Governance and Security Programme- Programme implementation action plan 2020/21-2025/26'), and one in Ethiopia ('3 year Justice Transformation Plan integrating PCJ principles'). Attribution Note: Result not fully attributable to HiiL, but achieved via contribution.

title.narrative: MFA Security and Rule of Law Results Framework
Number of (formal/informal) justice institutions strengthened in terms of fairness, effectiveness, accountability or independence.

description.narrative: HiiL indicator: # of justice institutions/organizations adopt guideline based on the co-created implementation plan (also indicate # of justice practitioners working in the concerned field in these institutions/organizations)

comment.narrative: The Means of Verification consists of HiiL's final institutional adoption measurement report (scheduled for 2025), complemented by co-created implementation plans and institutional records showing the integration of guidelines into training or practice.

Key Outputs Achieved: The 'Ethiopian Land Justice Guidelines' were developed and published, bringing the total to four guidelines produced. Furthermore, a total of 1,248 individuals across 32 institutions (26 formal, 6 informal) in Nigeria, Ethiopia, and Tunisia were formally trained on these new guidelines. Outcome Measurement: The final assessment of institutional strengthening and adoption is formally scheduled for 2025 (Actual: 0) to ensure reliable measurement of long-term impact.

The Means of Verification consists of HiiL's final institutional adoption measurement report (scheduled for 2025), complemented by co-created implementation plans and institutional records showing the integration of guidelines into training or practice.

The initial period focused on preparatory research and laying the groundwork for developing evidence-based practices (Output). No guidelines were formally published, no implementation plans were finalized, and no institutions were trained (Actual: 0).

The Means of Verification consists of HiiL's final institutional adoption measurement report (scheduled for 2025), complemented by co-created implementation plans and institutional records showing the integration of guidelines into training or practice.

The preparatory phase continued, aligning evidence-based content with local justice needs. No guidelines were published, no implementation plans were finalized, and no institutions were trained during 2022 (Actual: 0).

The Means of Verification consists of HiiL's final institutional adoption measurement report (scheduled for 2025), complemented by co-created implementation plans and institutional records showing the integration of guidelines into training or practice.

Three evidence-based guidelines were published (two in Nigeria and one in Tunisia), completing a key Output. Formal activities to measure the actual Outcome of institutional strengthening (adoption) are postponed to 2024/2025 to allow institutions time for internal planning and implementation (Actual: 0).
